channel.title: Writing
channel.description: Muhammad Hassan Raza runs product and engineering at Entropy Labs, builds backend and AI systems that hold up in production, and gets patches merged into open-source tools like kitty, calibre and libtorrent.

item.title: The Best Way to Learn a Codebase Is to Break Someone Else's
item.description: What maintainers of kitty, calibre, libtorrent and Fallow taught me in review threads, usually by explaining why my fix was wrong in a way I hadn't considered.

item.title: Every Abstraction I Regret
item.description: A short list of abstractions I added too early, why they got worse over time, and the heuristics I use now to avoid repeating it.

item.title: How Fallow Analyzes TypeScript in Under a Second
item.description: How Fallow gets dead-code and dependency analysis done fast by skipping the TypeScript compiler, flattening graph storage, and leaning on Rust.

item.title: Scoring Fraud in Legal Intake Calls
item.description: Coached callers, invented doctors and borrowed photos. How RISQ scores intake calls for mass tort firms, and why the most useful score measures the interviewer, not the caller.

item.title: How Pyscn Analyzes Python with Go and tree-sitter
item.description: How Pyscn uses Go and tree-sitter to analyze Python code quickly for dead code, clone detection, and dependency insight.

item.title: Agent Middleware: What Kept Obelisk's Agents in Line
item.description: Obelisk runs more than fifteen specialist agents. The agents were the easy part. Model choice, context, cost, retries and approvals all ended up in a middleware layer, and that layer is what made it work.

item.title: LLMs Can't Save Bad UX
item.description: When an AI feature flops, the model is rarely the problem. Three features I watched fail, what fixed them, and the questions I now ask before anyone writes a prompt.

item.title: Most of My Pull Requests Started as an Annoyance
item.description: Drive-by fixes in qBittorrent, Dokploy and django-hijack: which ones merged, which didn't, and what the rejections taught me about scope.

item.title: Structured Logging for AI Debugging
item.description: Why one structured event per request makes AI-assisted debugging far more useful than a pile of scattered console logs.

item.title: TF-IDF in OCaml: When Functional Programming Clicks
item.description: Building a local code search engine in OCaml turned out to be a good excuse to learn TF-IDF, pure pipelines, and where immutability actually helps.

item.title: I Shipped a Race Condition That Oversold Stock (And Other War Stories)
item.description: Two cashiers selling the last item, a chain that returned nothing, and a lock that only worked when both requests hit the same process. Bugs I shipped, and the unexciting fixes that held.

item.title: LangChain in Production: What the Tutorials Leave Out
item.description: Where LangChain earns its place, where it gets in the way, and the handful of habits that kept our AI features from failing quietly: timeouts, validation, real persistence, tracing and pinned versions.

item.title: Free Web Dev Platforms That Are Actually Worth Your Time
item.description: A practical shortlist of free web development learning platforms and how to use them without getting stuck in tutorials.

item.title: Final Year Project (FYP) Guide for Students
item.description: A practical final year project guide for choosing scope, building steadily, avoiding weak ideas, and presenting work clearly.

item.title: What I Actually Spend on Running mhassan.dev: $8/year
item.description: The full cost of running this site, what's free, and the tradeoffs behind each choice.

item.title: The Invoice Page That Took 4 Seconds to Search
item.description: How preloading product data cut search latency from 4 seconds to instant on a POS invoice page, and when this pattern breaks down.

item.title: When to Extract a Component (and When to Just Copy-Paste)
item.description: The 3-usage-sites heuristic for component extraction, a premature ConfirmDialog that cost me time, and why copy-paste is sometimes the right call in Vue.

item.title: Polaris Performance Log: The Django Mistakes I Made First
item.description: Refunds that queried once per line item, stock updated one row at a time, and signals that recalculated ledgers nobody asked about. What I changed in Polaris, and what I'd tell myself earlier.
